implementation_notes: Android default: the entity is an ordinary data class annotated with @Entity/@PrimaryKey/@ColumnInfo, and Room's symbol processor (KSP or kapt) reads that metadata at build time and generates the DAO and database code - so no reflection runs at runtime and the data class carries no persistence calls; the generated DAO is the mapper. Data classes keep equals/copy for domain use, which is exactly the lightweight shape. Classic hand-written Cursor mapping is only justified for queries that must be hand-tuned; on the JVM server side the Exposed variant is the usual choice.
pitfalls: Immutable data classes need default values (or a secondary no-arg constructor) for Room to instantiate them on load.
Generated schema changes require a migration: renaming a column without bumping the schema version fails at runtime, not at compile time.
Suspending DAO calls must not run on the main thread; a mapper call placed in a UI path crashes through Room's main-thread check.

variants.name: Exposed table objects (JVM/server side)
variants.idiom_name: object Users : Table("users") with typed columns
variants.implementation_notes: Server-side Kotlin alternative: the table and its columns are declared in a singleton object extending Table (integer("id").autoIncrement(), varchar("email_address", 200)), while entity types stay ordinary data classes mapped at query time or used through Exposed's DAO Entity class. The mapping metadata lives in the table object, not in the entity, and the DSL composes type-safe SQL. Choose it for JVM services where the table object doubles as the query source.
pitfalls: The Table object and an entity data class are two declarations of one schema; nothing forces them to agree unless you use the DAO Entity flavour or explicit mappers.
Plain DSL queries return ResultRow rather than entities, so row-to-entity mapping becomes code you own.
